assessments.reasoning: Authenticity. The Association Prolog Heritage facsimile presents the official reference manual. The archive separately identifies the PrologIA June 1996 manual and links the heritage collection. Integrity. The independently retrieved public file matched the frozen SHA-256 98749908eb4c25b0de3e0747bded62448065d5dfcb07bd6b9872cc2a3ef7e9fd. Relevance and interpretation at Physical PDF page 8, Introduction, discussion of derived languages and the new Marseille Prolog member (printed p. 2). The discussion of derived languages and the new member on printed p. 2 explicitly gives Prolog IV its own design within the Marseille Prolog family. The discussion identifies its optimized compiler and constraint solvers, and describes Prolog IV among constraint-programming languages. Applicability. The cited author or publisher describes the same frozen historical or documented scope. Contradiction check. The manual separates Prolog IV from a Prolog III upgrade, treats ISO standardization as context and describes an independent constraint-programming design within the Marseille Prolog family. The dialect edge expresses that scoped design lineage.

challenge.method: Read the full derived-language discussion on printed p. 2 and compare the opening of the Introduction and the model in §2.1. Test Prolog IV as an upgrade of III, as ISO Prolog itself, or as a product unrelated to the Prolog lineage.
challenge.results: The manual separates Prolog IV from a Prolog III upgrade, treats ISO standardization as context and describes an independent constraint-programming design within the Marseille Prolog family. The dialect edge expresses that scoped design lineage.

limitations: The registry dialect relationship records the manual's variant boundary at June 1996.
Dialect is project vocabulary. The manual does not establish that arbitrarily chosen Prolog or Prolog III programs are compatible.
